texts: doha pls: you can put a crooked man on the scales a thousand times, he'll still weigh the same, people never change their nature

Write a doha that says one may polish and weigh a person's character as often as one likes with advice and punishment, but the nature he was born with stays unmoved, like scales that always settle in the same place.
The scales may be weighed again and again, but the born nature of a man is a weight that never lessens.
scales, unchanging nature
I spent ten years hoping my brother-in-law would stop being petty and selfish, but he is exactly what he was on the wedding day, and I'd love a doha about that.
doha pls: you can coat an arrow in gold but it still flies the same, same for people's nature

Compose a doha explaining that a crooked arrow does not become straight because it is plated with gold, and a person's inborn nature does not change because he wears fine robes or learns clever speech.
My cousin's gold chain looked splendid but turned his neck green, just like his charm covers a nature that never changes; please write a doha about it.
arrow, gold, born nature
The arrow, however finely gilded in gold, flies by the nature of its shaft; and so a man by the nature of his birth.
My grandfather said that a man's nature stays with him until the cremation ground, no matter how many vows he takes, and I saw this in my uncle; please write a doha.
cremation ground, nature stays
doha pls: people don't change their nature until they reach the cremation ground
Till the last pyre burns in the cremation ground, a man's nature walks beside him, unchanged and unashamed.
Please craft a couplet that says a person's inborn nature goes with him through every promise and every reform, and does not leave him until the final rites in the cremation ground.
I tried for years to reform my stubborn father with gentle words, like pouring milk on a mountain, and it changed nothing; could you write a doha about it?
The mountain may be bathed in milk for a hundred years, yet it stays as hard as ever and its nature stays its own.

Write a doha saying that you can pour milk on a mountain and let it flow for ages, but the mountain stays dark and hard, and a person with a hard born nature likewise stays unmoved by your soft efforts.
mountain, milk, unchanging
doha: you can wash a mountain in milk but it won't change, like how people are born
lock, nature, birth
My uncle swore a hundred times he'd stop lying, and each time the lock of his old habit snapped him back; please make a doha about it.
Write a doha that says the habits we are born with are like a lock that cannot be broken by sermons or force, and that only one who accepts his own nature can hope to guide it a little.
The lock on nature has no key that opens it; what is born in a man dies with him.
doha pls: a lock is made to keep things shut, and a man's nature is the same, locked in from birth
I want a doha that says no teacher, no punishment and no promise can alter a person's inborn nature, since it is part of him from birth, and wisdom lies in knowing this instead of hoping.
What is born within us stays, whether we dress it in silk or in sackcloth; the heart's first colour never fades.
nature never changes
My ex promised on every birthday he'd be different, and every year he was the same man with new excuses; please write a doha to help me accept it.
doha about how people can't really change who they are
Make me a doha that says a person may be weighed on the scales of reform, counsel and punishment, but his inborn nature returns to its place like the beam of the scales that always settles back.
scales, true nature
Many times the scales are weighed anew, yet the born nature settles where it always did.
My uncle keeps making promises to quit his cheating habit on the scales of his grocery stall, and yet each week it is the same; write a doha about it.
doha: even if you put your habits on the scales and promise to change, your nature remains the same
doha pls: people don't change, it's how they are born
My mother always said my sister was born with a temper and no marriage, no school, no sorrow would change it, and she's turned out to be right; write a doha about that.

Please write a doha that says whatever a person is born with, kindness or cruelty, patience or temper, remains with him through all his years, and that the world's advice only fades beside his nature.
inborn nature
What nature gave at birth no sermon takes away; each person returns to his ways.

Compose a doha that says no matter how much you advise, scold or plead, a man's inborn nature stays as it was, and the wise accept this and shape their expectations rather than waste their lives hoping.
nature does not change
Teach as you will, the nature within smiles softly and remains.
doha pls on why you can't change someone's basic nature
I spent a whole year trying to make my lazy roommate more disciplined, and he's the same man he was; make a doha out of my tired wisdom.
doha pls: a needle goes through fabric the same way each time, people are like that too, they don't change their nature
The needle stitches the same line in any hand; so a man's nature runs unchanged through every day.
needle, unchanging nature

Can you make a doha saying that a needle may be polished and gilded, but it will still pass through fabric only in its own way, and so a person's birth-nature persists through all his adornments and schooling.
My grandmother's needle always pierced the same spot in the same sleeve, and I thought, so does a man's nature repeat itself; please write a doha about that.
doha: a bridge can be repaired but not the water under it, nature is like that, you can't change it, and the cremation ground sees it all in the end
bridge, cremation ground, nature
Write a doha that says bridges are repaired and the cremation ground has seen every form of reform, yet the born nature of a man crosses unchanged from his first day to his final.
I stood on the bridge by the cremation ground thinking of my dead friend, who never changed even once in his life; write a doha about him.
The bridge is rebuilt, the cremation ground is rebuilt, but the nature that crosses them is the same.
Please compose a doha for those who marry hoping to reform their partner, saying that nature stays with a person long after the wedding vows and no love can pull it out of him like a weed.
The rain falls upon every field alike, but what lies within decides the crop.
unchanged nature
doha pls: you can't change someone by loving them, nature stays
I thought marriage would turn my boyfriend gentle, but he is the same hot-headed man, and I should have known; write a doha for others like me.
doha pls: a seed grows what it is meant to grow even under a perfect moon, people also stay what they were born
Pen a doha that says the seed contains the whole plant within it, and no moonlight or watering will make it become anything else, just as a person's inborn nature decides what he will grow into.
seed, moon, born nature
My sister's seed of anger was planted in her young, and even under the moon of her calmest night, it springs up; please write a doha about our stubborn natures.
Beneath the silver moon a seed becomes only what it was always meant to be; so also the heart.
Write a doha saying that the chakor bird cannot learn to love anything but the one it longs for and the lotus cannot bloom in a desert, so a person cannot be forced to go against his deepest nature.
doha pls: a chakor loves its far-off beloved and a lotus loves the dawn light, nobody can change what they love by birth
chakor, lotus, nature
In my village the old people say a chakor can never be taught to love the dark, and a lotus never to rest on dry land, which is how my son is with his poetry; write a doha.
The chakor longs for the moonbeam, the lotus for the dawn; what birth has set, no teaching undoes.
doha pls: a physician can cure bodies but not natures
physician, incurable nature
The physician cures the fever, but the nature of the patient, he cannot cure; it is the only illness that none can heal.
The doctor in our town said he could fix my father's blood pressure but not his temper, because that's his nature; please write a doha with the doctor's wisdom in it.
Compose a doha explaining that a physician may heal a fever and set a broken bone but cannot treat the nature a man is born with, because it is not a disease but the very ground of the person.
The parrot learns a hundred words, yet drinks the same dew; the learned man changes his speech, never his heart.
parrot, dew, nature
doha pls: a parrot repeats words but a parrot stays a parrot, it won't become a different bird in the dew
My pet parrot greets everyone the same way even after I taught it new words, and it still drinks the morning dew like always, and it made me think of people; write a doha.
I want a doha that says a parrot may learn the speech of men and recite holy verses, but it still lives and hungers like a parrot, and a man may recite wisdom while his nature stays unmoved.
The bee goes to the flower in every land; and the man, to his old nature, in every season.
doha pls: a bee will go to the sweet flower no matter where you put it, nature is like that
bee, unchanging nature
My friend's cousin left the village to become a city man, but a bee will always be a bee, and one sniff of village flowers brings back his old self; please write a doha.

Compose a doha that says a bee can be taken far from its hive and fed on other things, but it returns to flowers by instinct, and a person's nature too returns to its first course after every journey.
Write a doha that says no matter which road a person takes at the crossroads of life, he takes his born nature with him, for it is the traveller's first luggage and the last.
I moved to a new city, a new job, a new life, and found my old habits right behind me at the crossroads; please write a doha about that.
doha pls: at the crossroads you can choose any road but your nature goes along with you
At every crossroads a man may turn left or right, but his nature walks with him down both.
crossroads, unchanging self
doha pls: no physician can climb the mountain of your nature and change it
I'd like a doha that says a skilled physician can ease pain and prolong life but there is a high mountain he cannot cross, which is the born nature of a person, steady and unchanged.
A physician told my family that on the mountain trek he treats broken legs but never habits, because habits come from nature; please write a doha about it.
physician, mountain, nature
The physician climbs the mountain of the body, yet cannot reach the peak of the nature; that height is unconquered.
My neighbour is as sharp as a sword and his wife as sweet as jaggery, and after thirty years of marriage they are exactly the same; write a doha about nature that doesn't change.
The sword cuts by its edge and the jaggery sweetens by its nature; so each man acts by what he was born with.
Write a doha that says the sword does not become sweet by being dipped in jaggery, nor does jaggery become sharp by being rubbed on a sword, and likewise no one can change a person's inborn nature.
doha pls: a sword stays sharp, jaggery stays sweet, nobody changes their nature
sword, jaggery, nature
My uncle at sixty is the same hot-headed man he was at twenty, and our whole family has stopped hoping he will change; write a doha about it.
The years may pass in their hundreds, but the nature at the heart sleeps and wakes unchanged.
nature stays
Compose a doha saying that a person may grow old, grow wise in speech and soft in manner, but when the right moment comes, his old nature rises up as if no time had passed at all.
doha pls on how people never change deep down
true nature appears
doha: when pressure comes, your real nature shows, always
I want a doha that says in calm times a person may appear gentle and polite, but when anger or temptation arrives, his born nature breaks out and everyone sees what he truly is.
In calm hours the nature sleeps, in storms it wakes; then see, O see, the man himself.
Our manager was all smiles until the deadline came, and then the shouting started; I realised that was always who he was. Could you write a doha?
doha plz: a moth keeps flying into the glare no matter how often it gets burned, nature is like that
The moth is drawn to the glare by nature, and no warning of its elders can keep it; so the heart returns to its old desire.
My younger brother keeps going back to the same bad habit even after getting burned many times, just like a moth; could you make a doha of it?
moth, nature, desire
Give me a doha explaining that a moth, however often it is hurt, will keep circling the glare, and a person with a certain nature will return to his old patterns even after learning their cost.
At my uncle's funeral they wrapped him in a fine shroud and placed gold on his forehead, and I thought, he was the same man in life and still the same; make a doha.
doha: no matter how fancy the shroud or gold ornament, the nature underneath is the same
shroud, gold, true nature
Write a doha that says neither a shroud nor gold nor any wealth can hide or change what a man was born with, since the end of life reveals only the nature that was always there.
Wrapped in a shroud woven with gold, the man is still what his nature made him.
nature is destiny
What nature planted at the cradle, the grave will find fully grown.
Compose a doha explaining that a person's inborn nature appears in childhood and ripens in old age, and no education, no travel and no hardship will remove it, only reveal it more clearly.
After twenty years in the same office, I can predict exactly how my colleague will react to every situation, because he has never changed once; please write a doha.
doha pls: you can't teach an old dog new tricks, same with natures
Bend a person as you will, the nature springs back in the same way.
nature won't bend
Please craft a couplet that says a person may try to change his nature for a short time through effort and discipline, but when the effort ends, the old nature returns like a stretched string.
A friend of mine tried hard to become patient after meditation retreats, but in a week at his job he was shouting again; write a doha about that.
yo write a doha, someone's nature always comes back after a short break
Though the sword rest in a velvet sheath, the edge is an edge, and the nature of the wielder remains.
sword, true nature
My cousin got a degree, a fancy job and a suit, but one angry word from me and the old street fighter in him came out, like a sword drawn from a velvet sheath; write a doha.
doha pls: a sword stays a sword even if you decorate it, nature doesn't change
Write a doha saying that a sword resting in a fine decorated sheath is still a sword, and a person of rough nature dressed in fine manners is still rough underneath, waiting for his moment.
doha pls about how you have to accept people the way they are
Do not blame the wind for blowing, or the man for being what he is.
I told my brother a thousand times to quit gambling, and he promised every time; I've finally accepted that it's his nature and I can't fix it. Could you write a doha?
Compose a doha that says wise people stop trying to remake others and instead accept their nature as they accept the weather, deciding only how close to stand and how much to expect.
accept their nature
Make me a doha that says one can repaint a door and fit it with a new frame, but the person who lives behind it keeps his nature, and only his surroundings are different.
door, unchanging nature
My landlord renovated every door of the building but he's still the same stingy man, and I wrote a note to myself to remember this; please make a doha out of it.
The door can be repainted, the hinges oiled, but the one who walks through it remains himself.
doha pls: you can renovate the door but the person behind it doesn't change
doha pls: you can't fix someone's nature, just learn to live with it
My father stopped drinking twenty years ago, but his old anger still comes out at weddings, and we've all learned to read the signs; write a doha about it.
unchangeable nature

I want a doha that says people can repent, pray or try to reform themselves, yet the root of their temper, greed or kindness stays quietly beneath, and only wise watchfulness keeps it from ruling their lives.
Nature, once given, is a guest that never departs; welcome it or leave, but expect it not to go.
grindstone, rough nature
The old grindstone in our village mill wears down but never changes its rough nature, and my husband is the same; please write a doha.
Write a doha that says a grindstone is rough by its nature and, however long it is used, it will not become smooth, just as a person of rough character stays rough no matter how many years pass.
doha pls: a grindstone is rough from birth, same as some people
The grindstone grows thin with years but never soft; such is the nature of the stubborn heart.
What the cradle gave, the final rites find again; between the two, only the dress changes.
My teacher once said that she could tell a child's whole life by his behaviour at age five, and I've watched it come true over thirty years; please write a doha.
nature from birth
Compose a doha explaining that the nature a child shows in early years often remains with him throughout life, and parents should observe and guide it kindly rather than try to remake it completely.
doha plz: people show who they are early and never change
Born with a storm in the heart, the child grows to a man with the same storm; only the years give it a calmer name.
My niece had a sharp temper even as a baby, and even now at twenty she is the same, despite all the love we gave her; write a doha.
I want a doha that says the temper a person is born with is like a hidden weather in his heart; he may hide it, delay it, tame it a little, but he can never truly make it leave.
doha pls: some people are born angry, and no one can change that
inborn temper
hard natures, soft natures
doha: you can't make a soft person hard or a hard one soft
A sweet word cannot soften a hard nature, nor a hard word harden a soft one; each is its own.
Can you make a doha that says that a gentle person cannot be made cruel by hardship nor a cruel person made gentle by kindness, as each carries a nature that outlasts every training.
Tough as I tried to be in the army, my soft heart stayed soft, and others around me who learned kindness stayed hard; write a doha on nature.
My grandmother used to say that you can put sugar on a bitter gourd but it will still taste the same, and I think of her when my cousin never changes; write a doha.
Write a doha saying that a bitter gourd boiled in sugar or fried in oil will still taste bitter, and a person's inborn nature will show itself in the end whatever sweetness is put on top of it.
bitter gourd, nature
Though fried in ghee and sweet spice, the bitter gourd stays bitter; the born nature does not forget itself.
doha pls: you can sugarcoat a bitter gourd but it stays bitter, same as people's nature
I once tried to get a yogi friend to attend a wedding with a feast, but he sat in silence in a corner, as quiet as ever; please write a doha about people's nature.
doha pls: salt can't be made sweet and a yogi can't be made worldly, nature is nature
salt, yogi, nature
The salt is salt in any water; the yogi is a yogi in any city; none can unmake what birth has made.
Compose a doha that says salt cannot be sweetened by any amount of boiling and a yogi cannot be tempted to love wealth by any feast, because both keep their nature through every circumstance.
After my son was caught lying again, I realised he has always been like that, and I should guide him instead of punishing him; write a doha for me.
The wise know that no vow can undo what grew with the child; they forgive the nature and guard the household.
doha pls: you can't take away someone's nature, just watch for it
deep-rooted nature

I want a doha that says a person's nature is a root that grows with him, and wise parents, teachers and friends, instead of hoping to uproot it, learn to guide the growth gently and guard against its harm.
My neighbour's sharp tongue has stung this lane for thirty years, and no scolding or sorrow has dulled it; please write a doha about this.
Pen a doha that says the tongue reveals what the heart was born with, and a sweet tongue or a sharp one cannot easily be changed by lessons, because speech is only the nature coming out.
doha pls: a person's tongue shows their nature and it never changes
sharp tongue, nature
The tongue is the herald of the nature; speak to it, scold it, it will say the same in the end.
doha pls: a lamp gives light by its nature and nothing can make it give darkness
lamp, nature, unchanged
The lamp gives light because it is a lamp; the heart gives what it is.
My teacher is like a lamp; whatever the weather, whatever mood, she's the same kindly source of guidance; write a doha about natures that stay good.
Compose a doha that says the lamp's nature is to give light even in a storm, and a person of noble inborn nature stays noble through every trial, just as a person of base nature stays base.
Please write a doha saying that even a great sorrow or sudden fear may change a person for a short time, but soon the old nature returns and takes its seat, as if nothing had ever happened.
Everyone in my family said my uncle would never change after the accident, and they were right; write a doha about how habits stay with people.
return to nature
The mind may be shaken clean by sorrow, yet its first habit returns and sits down in the old place.
doha: people go back to being themselves, always
I want a doha that says every person carries a nature as deep as his bones, and that sermons, books, teachers and travel only touch the surface, while the core stays as it was when he was born.
doha about how some people just are who they are
I tried to cheer up my moody friend for ten years; today he is just as moody, and I've finally accepted that this is who he is. Write a doha.
character is fixed
As the colour of the eye is not changed by seeing, so the heart is not changed by learning.
Write a doha saying that a person who goes far away to change his life finds that he has taken his nature along, for it is a part of himself and stays near him wherever he travels.
carry your nature
Though you cross the farthest waters, you carry yourself with you; the nature lives where you live.
After the best therapist and the longest vacation, my husband was still the same worrier he was before, and I had to laugh; please write a doha about that.
doha: natures don't change with holidays or lessons
The elephant is bound by a single thread of habit, yet his nature remains vast and untamed.

Compose a doha explaining that an elephant held by a thin thread stays only because of belief, and the moment it chooses, its wild nature returns and the thread breaks, just as a man's nature breaks all weak restraints.
doha pls: you can tie an elephant with a thread but it won't change its nature, it'll just pull when it wants
My brother's rage is like an elephant, held back by a thin thread of our mother's love, but nothing changes his nature; write a doha about it.
thread, elephant, nature
I'd like a doha that says a stone left in the stream for a hundred years is smooth outside but unchanged inside, and a person may show a polished face while his old nature lives on beneath it.
I carved a small statue out of a stone that the stream had polished for ages, and the inside was just as hard as before, which reminded me of my stubborn uncle; write a doha.
The stone lies in the stream for a thousand years and is still stone within; so is a man who bathes in advice.
doha pls: a stone left in the stream for a century is still hard inside, people are like that too
stone, nature
Compose a doha that says the elephant, however carefully bathed, throws dust on himself the moment he leaves the water, and so a person washed by advice and pilgrimage returns to his original nature.
The elephant bathes at the ford and then tosses dust upon his back; so the man returns to his habit.
doha pls: the elephant always throws dust on its head even after a bath, natures don't change
elephant, bathing, nature
After the bath, my uncle's elephant immediately threw dust over its back, and I laughed, because my husband always spoils a clean room in the same way; write a doha.
born nature
Please write a doha that says education, family and environment can polish a person, yet deep inside there is a nature with which he came into the world, and that is the true colour of his soul.
The deep root of nature no axe of advice can cut; the fruit it bears is its own.
My two sons were raised in the same family, with the same rules, and yet one is gentle and one is quick-tempered; I'd like a doha about how nature is not something you can raise into someone.
doha pls on inborn nature, short and clear
A yogi came to our gate and mended my torn sleeve with a needle in a minute, remaining as calm as ever though we offered him wealth; write a doha about such unchanging nature.
yogi, needle, steadfast nature
doha pls: a yogi can't change his calm nature and a needle can't change its sharp one, both stay as they are

Give me a doha that says the yogi's quiet nature is like a needle that pierces without bending, because it will not be altered by wealth, praise or fear, as it was shaped long before the world could touch it.
A needle passes through the fabric, and the yogi through the world, both unmoved in their nature.
The old man outside the shrine looked saintly like a heron but kept his hand out for coins, while a young diamond-seller in our town gave kindly; their natures never changed, write a doha.
The heron stands as if in prayer, the diamond rests in the dust; each keeps the nature it was made with.
Compose a doha that says a heron remains hungry beneath its calm, and a diamond remains hard under any hammer, and so a person's essential nature shows through every costume that he puts on.
heron, diamond, nature
doha pls: a heron looks holy but stays a heron, and a diamond stays hard in any hand
Write a doha saying that time is a touchstone for human nature, and whatever mask a man wears, the test shows his true colour, which is the colour of his birth, unchanged and unhidden.
The old goldsmith in our village could judge a man's nature by watching him at the touchstone, and said it never changed with years; please write a doha.
touchstone, true nature
doha pls: the touchstone shows the real thing and so does time, natures don't change
The touchstone shows the colour of metal, and time shows the colour of a man; neither is ever altered.

Please craft a couplet explaining that a moth does not change its nature even when its wings are scorched, and that a person whose nature draws him to danger or folly goes back to it though he knows the pain.
The moth knows the end and still goes forward; the nature is stronger than the knowing.
My sister knows that her habit of spending is hurting her, yet she can't stop herself, like a moth; could you write a doha about it?
moth, nature
doha pls: a moth keeps going back to the light even after it gets burnt, it can't help its nature
